zeroEngine.policy: unverified-by-default; preserve existing integrated Scheduler; adaptively inject into recognized user init.lua; optional core-profiler fallback leaves 0-Engine completely untouched

managerChanges: two-page setup keeps optional frame-time pairing separate from CET/0-Engine installation and recovery
optional frame-time companion detection is read-only; CapFrameX start-key detection recognizes CaptureHotKey without modifying CapFrameX
companion captures are copied into the CET archive under FrameTime and are never deleted from their source
single CETProfiler_Toggle input defaults to F11
first F11 starts a fresh measurement; second F11 stops and automatically exports CET results
known CET runtime output patterns are copied, verified, then removed from the live CET folder; unrelated files are never swept
CET binding state is stored inside the persistent game-side profiler state and restored transactionally
standalone RESULTS remain package-local; TOTAL Profiler does not redirect profiler-owned output paths
0-Engine core-only mode is presented as a fallback only when safe Scheduler integration is unavailable or fails
Core profiler fallback leaves the user's 0-Engine folder and Scheduler completely untouched and loaded normally
recognized unintegrated/custom 0-Engine versions are patched transactionally using their own init.lua
adaptive mode uses unique modules/CETProfilerScheduler.lua to avoid colliding with 0-Engine Scheduler.lua
existing PASS/Scheduler-integrated 0-Engine keeps the proven Scheduler.lua swap path
CETProfilerControls remains temporary profiler-owned UI and is removed on restore
